context: Decide the intended contract: either extend compliance classification to TPC-H and TPC-DI so published results carry a comparable methodology guarantee, or record explicitly why TPC-DS alone is gated and document that TPC-H results are unqualified. Do not extend the gate without deciding what happens to the 22 existing TPC-H bundles already in the public corpus, which were minted with no compliance field.
description: Observed 2026-08-18 while fixing the TPC-DS compliance wiring. TPC-DS classifies every run (benchbox/core/tpcds/compliance.py) and benchbox submit refuses unofficial_nonstandard and unofficial_subscale results. TPC-H and TPC-DI have no equivalent: grep for compliance_class across benchbox/core/tpch/ and benchbox/core/tpcdi/ returns nothing, and TPC-H bundles carry no compliance_class field at all. Confirmed empirically: tpch_sf10_duckdb_sql_20260817_210939_80e1274f and tpch_sf100_duckdb_sql_20260817_214011_d40cb760 both pass benchbox submit without ever being run with --official. The consequence is that a casually configured TPC-H run publishes to the corpus with exactly the same standing as a rigorous one, while an equally rigorous TPC-DS run is refused unless it was invoked with --official. Whichever way this is resolved, the current asymmetry means the corpus mixes results whose methodology guarantees differ without any field distinguishing them - which matters most for TPC-H, the benchmark the corpus has most of.

verifications.expected: states which benchmarks are gated and why
